slides.title: Requirement-Driven Design of Whole-Body Social Tactile Sensing via Virtual Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework to derive tactile sensing requirements from interaction data, supporting the development of social robots capable of recognizing human touch gestures.

card.one_liner: A framework using VR to derive robot tactile sensor placement and resolution requirements before hardware fabrication.
card.key_idea: VR-based interaction data allows offline reconstruction of contact geometry, enabling simulation of various sensor layouts and resolutions to optimize gesture recognition accuracy without physical prototypes.
card.evaluation: Tested on 18 participants with 5,520 trials across 8 gestures. Used Random Forest and CNN-GRU classifiers with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.
card.limitation: Simulation uses binary contact signals only (no force/pressure) and was evaluated exclusively on a single robot's arm.

slides.title: Whole-Body Semantic-to-Actuation Grounding of Elephant-Inspired Soft-Trunk Motion via Lightweight Flow Matching
slides.highlight: This work presents a framework for grounding open-vocabulary responses into whole-body motions for a soft-trunk robot, enhancing user satisfaction in human-robot interaction. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A framework grounding MLLM responses into expressive, whole-body soft-trunk motions using lightweight flow matching.
card.key_idea: Uses morphology-aligned intent-intensity tuples and Catmull-Rom spline controls to reduce dimensionality, then employs a rectified-flow generator for efficient, diverse, and executable actuation trajectory sampling.
card.evaluation: Ablations showed 77.2% correctness (vs 25% baseline) and 4.87ms inference. A 100-participant study increased positive satisfaction from 46% to 82%.
card.limitation: The physical HRI study compared grounded motion against an audiovisual-only baseline rather than manually scripted trunk motions.

slides.title: TactiDex: A Real-World Tactile-Guided Benchmark for Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: TactiDex introduces a real-world benchmark and the TactiSkill framework to move robotic dexterous manipulation from kinematic mimicry toward physically grounded, tactile-aware interaction.

card.one_liner: TactiDex is a tactile-rich benchmark and framework for transferring human-like dexterous manipulation to robots.
card.key_idea: TactiSkill uses a tri-component tactile reward (guidance, alignment, and safety constraints) to move beyond kinematic mimicry toward physically grounded, force-aware robotic interaction.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 73 sequences using kinematic and tactile metrics; TactiSkill outperformed baselines in tactile-aware success (64.64%) and safety (SafeTac@3N: 53.57%).

slides.title: Robust In-Hand Manipulation via Priors in Reinforcement Learning and Mechanical Design
slides.tldr: PHYSICS PRIORS FOR ROBUST IN-HAND ROLLING
slides.highlight: This work combines a global grasp-quality reward and local fingertip curvature priors to improve rotation efficiency and stability in multifingered robotic manipulation.

card.one_liner: Improves robust in-hand rotation by combining grasp-quality RL rewards with anisotropic fingertip mechanical design.
card.key_idea: Integrates a global grasp-quality prior (minimum eigenvalue of the grasp map) as a dense RL reward and a local contact-geometry prior via cylindrical fingertip morphology.
card.evaluation: Tested on cylinders, cuboids, and balls across four palm orientations using an Allegro Hand; measured rotation speed, duration, and success rate in sim-to-real.
card.limitation: Not evaluated on translation or tool-use; robustness tested primarily via gravity changes rather than direct external perturbations.

slides.title: TAC-LOCO: Unified Whole-Body Control for Quadrupedal TACtile-Informed LOCO-Manipulation
slides.tldr: TACTILE-AUGMENTED REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FOR QUADRUPEDAL LOCO-MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This framework integrates tactile array observations with proprioception to enable unified whole-body control of legs, arms, and grippers. It allows robots to regulate grasp force and prevent object slip during dynamic movement under uncertain external forces.

card.one_liner: TAC-LOCO enables quadruped robots to adaptively regulate grasp force during dynamic loco-manipulation using tactile feedback.
card.key_idea: A unified RL framework encoding tactile array observations into compact latents, jointly controlling legs, arm, and gripper via a shared-backbone MLP with advantage-mixing for coordinated whole-body motion.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation and zero-shot deployment on Unitree Go2; achieved 90% hardware success rate, <1% drop rate, and 47% reduction in grasping force.
card.limitation: Imperfect simulation of gripper deformation prevents absolute force thresholding; servo-controlled arm dynamics limit potential dynamic performance.

slides.title: VistaVLA: Geometry- and Semantic-Aware 3D Gaussian-Grounded VLA for Robotic Manipulation
slides.highlight: VistaVLA utilizes 3D Gaussian primitives to create a geometry- and semantics-aware cognitive representation, supporting the MOSAIC goal of integrating ego-exo views and spatial layouts for robotic control.

card.one_liner: VistaVLA enhances robotic manipulation by grounding VLA models in a semantic, 3D Gaussian-based cognitive representation.
card.key_idea: Lifts multi-view features into 3D Gaussian primitives and uses a Merge-then-Query (MtQ) mechanism to compress dense primitives into 64 compact, spatially anchored context tokens.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on seven real-world tasks and LIBERO simulation. Results show a 22.8% real-world success rate gain and superior OOD robustness over VLA-Adapter.
card.limitation: Limited to tabletop manipulation with fixed robot platforms and requires calibrated multi-view cameras and posed observations.

slides.title: A Minimalist Retargeting-Guided Reinforcement Learning Recipe for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces REGRIND, a pipeline that learns dexterous manipulation policies from a single human demonstration. It is relevant to RwB for its application of human-to-robot motion retargeting to achieve fluid, human-like behavior in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: Regrind learns dexterous manipulation policies from a single human demonstration using interaction-preserving motion retargeting.
card.key_idea: Retargets human motion via interaction meshes to preserve hand-object spatial relationships, then trains a residual RL policy in simulation using augmented reference trajectories and reference state initialization.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on scissors and screwdriver tasks using LEAP and WUJI hands. Metrics include object tracking error and success rate; results show reliable zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.
card.limitation: Requires motion capture for object state at deployment and careful system identification to bridge the sim-to-real gap.

slides.title: DexVerse: A Modular Benchmark for Multi-Task, Multi-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: DexVerse provides a large-scale testbed for multi-task and multi-embodiment manipulation, supporting the ADAM-CHAT goal of evaluating agents in complex, diverse interaction environments.

card.one_liner: DexVerse is a modular benchmark for multi-task, multi-embodiment dexterous manipulation featuring 100 diverse tasks.
card.key_idea: A configuration-driven simulation framework supporting 3 robot arms, 6 dexterous hands, and configurable visual variations, paired with 3,180 VR-teleoperated multi-modal demonstrations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated Diffusion Policy, DP3, OpenVLA, and π0.5 across 19 tasks; best baselines achieved only 34% mean success rate, showing significant gaps in precision.
card.limitation: Current policies struggle with sub-centimeter alignment and sustained force regulation, with several tight-tolerance tasks achieving zero success.
